title: Effects of caffeine on anxiety and panic attacks in patients with panic disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis

claims.statement: In adults with panic disorder diagnosed by a clinician and tested in laboratories while off psychiatric medicines, a single oral dose of caffeine of 400 to about 750 mg (480 mg in 7 of 10 studies; study conditions), compared with a placebo of the same or similar taste in the same people, increases the chance of a panic attack within hours, by a meta-analysis of 10 small blinded challenge studies published from 1985 to 2015 (Klevebrant & Frick, 2022): in the 9 studies that reported panic attacks, 121 of 237 people with panic disorder (51 in 100) had one after caffeine, and no study reported one after placebo; in the 6 studies that also tested people without panic disorder, 69 of 128 people with panic disorder (54 in 100) had one after caffeine against 2 of 115 healthy controls (2 in 100), a difference of 52 in 100 (editors' calculation). The paper prints two incompatible pooled risk ratios for that comparison (about 32 by its text and 12.1 in its figure), so the counts are the better summary. Self-rated anxiety rose after caffeine in both groups, more on average in people with panic disorder (standardized difference 1.02, 95% CI 0.09 to 1.96), but the studies varied widely (prediction interval −1.27 to 3.32; about 0.72 without one outlying study, editors' recalculation), and these rises were measured after caffeine without a placebo comparison, which only 2 studies reported. The authors equate 480 mg with about 5 cups of brewed coffee at about 100 mg a cup, so the doses tested correspond to about 4 to 7.5 such cups taken at once (editors' calculation); no study tested less than 400 mg, so what everyday amounts do in panic disorder is not known. All studies were done at rest during a break from psychiatric medicines; 2 always gave caffeine last, and 8 of the 10 come from two research groups. Certainty: low. Status: replicated.
claims.magnitude: Klevebrant & Frick (2022): panic attacks after caffeine 121/237 (51.1%) with panic disorder in 9 studies and 2/115 (1.7%) controls; none after placebo in any study. In the 6 studies with both groups 69/128 (53.9%) against 2/115 (1.7%), risk difference 52.2 percentage points (editors' calculation); pooled log RR 3.47 (95% CI 2.06 to 4.87) in the text, which is RR about 32 (7.8 to 130; editors' calculation), against RR 12.12 (6.06 to 24.23) in Fig. 4. Studies without controls: 52/109 (47.7%). Anxiety change after caffeine (6 studies; 121 with panic disorder, 111 controls): g 1.94 (1.19 to 2.69) and 0.91 (0.46 to 1.36); difference g 1.02 (0.09 to 1.96), I² 66.8%, prediction interval −1.27 to 3.32; about 0.72 (0.07 to 1.37) without the outlying study (editors' recalculation). Doses 400 to about 750 mg, about 4 to 7.5 cups of brewed coffee at about 100 mg a cup (editors' calculation from the authors' equivalence of 480 mg with about 5 cups).
